To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) mean substitution is a flawed method for handling missing cases and (b) both multiple imputation methods and full information maximum-likelihood methods are recommended alternatives to mean substitution.

mean substitution is an inferior method for handling missingness in counseling psychology research; that multiple imputation and maximum likelihood estimation are recommended methods for dealing with missingness; and that counseling psychology researchers should be encouraged to report the amount and nature of missing data and how they handled those data.

(a) the amount and pattern (missing completely at random, MCAR; missing at random, MAR; or not missing at random, NMAR) of missing data should be reported, and (b) the method of handling the missing data should be described.
